This bar covers the states of North Africa and West Asia after the Ottoman Empire fell: Turkey, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Syria, Lebanon, Jordan, Israel and their neighbours. Many of their borders were drawn by Britain and France after 1918.

During the First World War, Britain and France secretly agreed in the Sykes-Picot Agreement to divide the Ottoman Arab lands. After the war the League of Nations gave them "mandates": Britain took Iraq, Palestine and Transjordan, France took Syria and Lebanon. Turkey fought off partition and became a republic in 1923. Egypt won nominal independence in 1922, Iraq in 1932, and Ibn Saud united most of Arabia as Saudi Arabia in 1932.

Main threads since:

  • Oil. Huge fields in Iran, Iraq and the Gulf, worked first by Western firms like Aramco, made the region central to the world economy. Producers formed OPEC in 1960, and the 1973 embargo showed their power.
  • Israel and Palestine. The founding of Israel in 1948 and the Nakba began a conflict that produced wars in 1956, 1967, 1973 and later.
  • Arab nationalism. Nasser of Egypt led a wave of army officers who overthrew kings in the 1950s and 1960s.
  • Political Islam. The Iranian Revolution of 1979 set up a Shia theocracy and inspired Islamist movements elsewhere.
  • War and upheaval. The Iran-Iraq war, the Gulf wars, the Arab Spring of 2011 and the civil wars in Syria, Libya and Yemen that followed.
